flags.reason: The random RFID split takes test indices from all_indices[:num_test] instead of all_indices[num_train:], so every test sample is also in the training set for the default 80/20 split.
The BLE random split takes both train and test sets from the start of the same shuffled array, making the entire default test set a subset of training.
fourier_loss detaches pred before the FFT, so the configured Fourier term contributes no gradient while still reducing the L1 coefficient in the total loss.

eval_fle derives its parameter count from the full coefficient tensor and uses deg only in assertions, so active_fle_degree and the documented progressive degree ramp do not change the rendered model.
CSI rendering requires 52 signal channels, but GaussianModel defaults to 2 and the CSI config never sets num_channels_override, making the reshape/output contract invalid.
The README advertises two-phase CSI training through main_csi.py, but that training entry point is absent.
The README documents CSI inference with inference_csi.py, but no such inference implementation is included.
The README documents pretrained BLE inference with inference_ble.py, but the file is absent.
The README's primary CSI command is bash run_csi.sh, but that launcher is absent.
render_rfid reads T_rx but never uses it, so predictions are invariant to receiver/gateway position for a fixed transmitter and model.
render_csi likewise reads but never uses the receiver/antenna position T_rx, despite CSI being defined per base-station antenna.
GaussianModel looks for _fle_init_scale on itself but never copies it from args, so the RFID/BLE configured initialization scales are ignored in favor of 0.1.
BLE training forcibly sets gene_init_point=True for the first gateway, contradicting and bypassing the config value false.
CSI normalization means and variances are computed over the full dataset before splitting, leaking test-set statistics into training.
The optimizer step is skipped on the final iteration, so the gradient computed for the advertised final iteration is never applied.
BLE also skips optimizer.step on the final iteration while saving and evaluating beforehand, so the final gradient is discarded and checkpoints are pre-update states.

At non-final checkpoints the PLY and validation are produced before optimizer.step while the same-numbered checkpoint is written after it, so artifacts with one iteration label represent different model states.
The documented environment omits pandas even though BLE loading imports it unconditionally, so the advertised setup is insufficient for BLE training.
CSI samples contain no transmitter coordinates, so the advertised autoencoder phase has no supervision tying its 3D latent to actual TX positions rather than an arbitrary reconstruction code.
The official RFID launcher relies on grep -P, which is unsupported by standard BSD/macOS grep and makes the documented workflow non-portable.
